en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Rattandhakāravagga 18.
The Training Rule on Causing Others to Be Reprimanded.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a nun who was a pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī was attending upon Bhaddā Kāpilānī with great care.
Bhaddā Kāpilānī said this to the nuns:
"Ladies, this nun attends upon me with great care; I shall give her a robe."
Then that bhikkhunī, having misapprehended and misinterpreted [the matter], complained about another, saying:
"I suppose, noble lady, that I do not attend upon you properly; I suppose the noble lady will not give me a robe.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How indeed can a bhikkhunī, on account of what was wrongly grasped and poorly investigated, cause another to be censured?
… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that a bhikkhunī, on account of what was wrongly grasped and poorly investigated, causes another to be censured?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How, monks, can a bhikkhunī, on account of what is wrongly grasped and wrongly understood, cause another to be censured?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence…” [and so forth].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“If a nun, on account of what is wrongly grasped or wrongly understood, should cause another to be annoyed, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“If any nun” means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a bhikkhunī" ...pe...
this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"By a wrong grasp" means by grasping otherwise.
"By a misinterpretation" means...
If one censures another who has received full ordination based on what was perceived otherwise, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she complains against one who is fully ordained, perceiving her as fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she complains against one who is fully ordained, being in doubt, there is an offense of expiation.
If she complains against one who is fully ordained, perceiving her as not fully ordained, there is an offense of expiation.
If one reviles one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one perceives as fully ordained one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one is doubtful regarding one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is not fully ordained, and she perceives her as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense for one who is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the eighth training rule.
